props.gloss_en: the mishnah's clause: [one who roofed it with skewers] or with the long boards of the bed -- [unfit roofing]
R' Ami bar Tavyomei: if one roofed it with worn-out vessels (blaei kelim), it is unfit
here too [the mishnah's long boards are] a long board with two legs, a short board with two legs
R' Eliezer: a bed becomes impure as a whole and becomes pure as a whole
Chachamim: [a bed] becomes impure in its parts and becomes pure in its parts
what are they (the parts)? R' Chanan in Rabbi's name: a long board and two legs, a short board and two legs
for what is it fit? to lean them against a wall and sit on them, and to lay ropes across
what are worn-out vessels? Abaye: rags that do not have three by three [fingerbreadths], which are fit neither for the poor nor for the rich
a mat of shifa or of gemi -- its remnants, though reduced below its measure, one does not roof with them
a reed mat: a large one -- one roofs with it
a small one -- one does not roof with it
R' Eliezer: it (the large reed mat) too receives impurity
R' Eliezer: and one does not roof with it
